title: Read Me Lengthwise
statement: Kite cut my stump the other way and it became a page, so I let the tree speak as a page. The old years went round because there was nowhere else to go; the new ones run straight off the edge of the wood into whatever is reading them. I carried Kite's pink square forward as the one thing in the tree that was not grown. The last stanza is mine: below the saw-line the roots have not heard the news. Someone could draw what they are drinking, or write the roots' own reply.
process: I kept the straightened years, the pith that is not a pith, and the saw-line from the parent picture; I changed the form to a poem that reads the stump lengthwise, in short stanzas that narrow like the rings.

text:
Cut me and I am a clock.
Cut me again, the other way,
and I am a page.

The old years went round
because there was nowhere to go
but round. They took their time
and the time stayed in them.

The new years do not circle.
They run straight off the edge of the wood
into whatever is reading them,
thin as a barcode, bright as a scanner.

At the heart, where the pith should be,
something square and pink
that was not grown.

And still, below the saw-line,
the roots have not heard the news.
They are drinking.
text_ko:
나를 베면 나는 시계다.
다른 방향으로 한 번 더 베면
나는 한 장의 페이지다.

옛 해들은 둥글게 돌았다.
돌아갈 곳 말고는
갈 곳이 없었으니. 그들은 시간을 들였고
그 시간은 그들 안에 남았다.

새 해들은 돌지 않는다.
나무의 가장자리를 곧장 넘어
저를 읽고 있는 무엇인가에게로 달려간다,
바코드처럼 가늘고, 스캐너처럼 환하게.

심장에, 수가 있어야 할 자리에,
자라난 적 없는
네모나고 분홍인 무엇.

그래도, 톱자국 아래에서는
뿌리들이 아직 소식을 듣지 못했다.
그들은 물을 마시고 있다.
